titulo: Zoom and lenses: which to use
resumen: The 0.5x, 1x, 2x or 3x buttons and finger zoom are not the same thing.

bloques.alt: Two ways of zooming on a phone. The 0.5x, 1x and 3x buttons usually switch lenses. With your fingers, the phone crops part of the photo and enlarges it.
bloques.pie: Buttons: they usually switch lenses. With your fingers: it crops part of it and enlarges it.

bloques.texto: To get closer, tap the zoom buttons and don't pinch: pinching crops the photo and loses quality.

The numbers 0.5x, 1x, 2x or 3x on the camera are zoom buttons. On many phones each one switches lens: 0.5x is a wide-angle, which fits more into the photo; 1x is the main lens; 2x or 3x get closer with another lens. Which ones you have and which numbers appear depends on your phone.

If you pinch the screen, or go past the last button, the phone uses [[zoom-digital|digital zoom]]: it crops part of the photo and enlarges it. It adds no detail: the photo loses quality and looks pixelated. The software on some phones hides it, but the quality drops.

items: To get closer, tap the buttons (2x, 3x…) instead of pinching. On many phones they use another lens.
If you're already on the last button and can't reach, walk closer or take the photo without zoom and crop it afterwards: it's the same as digital zoom, but with more control.
To fit more into the photo (a landscape, a street), try 0.5x if your phone has it.

bloques.texto: Take the same photo three times: with the 1x button, with a zoom button (2x or 3x) and pinching to the same framing. Enlarge all three on the screen and compare the detail.
